AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 7, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL
MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION.
TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING, ATTEND THE MEETING IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS,
SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING:
(669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685 DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK
ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON
THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING - 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: 13400 San Antonio Drive/APNS 8056-015-014, 8056-015-016, and 8056-015-020;
  Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and Michael F G Trust;
  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Arthur McKibben
  Norwalk Church of the Nazarene

FLAG SALUTE
  Julio De La Hoya
  Youth Commissioner/Summer Youth Worker

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Los Angeles County Health Department presentation regarding the Vaccine Clinic.

  3.  Chipotle Grand Opening.

  4.  Community Clean Up Recap.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of August
  17 and 23, 2021. 825-04
   Report

2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period July 25, 2021 – August
  7, 2021, in the total amount of $922,688.11. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  August 12, 2021 - August 25, 2021, in the total amount of $3,410,398.31. 640

  Report

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Leslie Cruz,
  Ana Guevara, Terrance Johnson, and Samantha Perez. 830-03/07/16

  Report

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – AUGUST 25, 2021 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

6.  PROJECT NOS. 7228 AND 7230 – RESOLUTION NOS. 21-53 AND 21-54 – BUDGET AMENDMENTS
  – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-53, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE MEASURE “R” BOND PROCEEDS TO PROJECT NO.
  7228 - TRAFFIC SIGNAL IMPROVEMENTS ON ROSECRANS AVENUE, FROM STUDEBAKER
  ROAD TO CARMENITA ROAD; and

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 21-54, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE MEASURE “R” BOND PROCEEDS TO PROJECT NO.
  7230 - TRAFFIC SIGNAL IMPROVEMENTS ALONG SAN ANTONIO DRIVE FROM ROSECRANS
  AVE TO CIVIC CENTER DRIVE AT BLOOMFIELD AVENUE. 610/1005-04-7228/7230

  Report

7.  PROJECT NO. 3302-2021 - ACCEPT WORK FOR CITYWIDE ANNUAL SIDEWALK/CONCRETE
  REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT– ENGINEERS REPORT 21-18 – Staff recommends the City Council
  accept the work of CJ Concrete Construction, Inc. in the amount of $211,057 for citywide annual
  sidewalk/concrete repair and replacement and curb ramp installations to comply with Americans with
  Disabilities Act standards. 1005-04-3302-2021

  Report

8.  PROJECT NO. 7926.1 - ACCEPT WORK FOR LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM -
  CONCRETE IMPROVEMENTS AT ZONE 32 (ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 21-19) - Staff recommends
  City Council accept the work by CJ Concrete Construction, Inc. for $548,217.56 for Project No. 7926.1,
  the Local Street Rehabilitation Program - Concrete Improvements Zone 32. 1005-04-7926.1

  Report

9.  REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR RELAY FOR LIFE EVENT – Staff recommends
  City Council approve the event requested by Relay for Life committee for October 23, 2021. 920-01-02

  Report

10. RESOLUTION NO. 21-56 - APPROVAL OF DISADVANTAGED BUSINESS ENTERPRISE (DBE)
  THREE YEAR GOAL FOR FEDERAL FISCAL YEARS 2022 THROUGH 2024 - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 21-56, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
   NORWALK ESTABLISHING AN OVERALL DISADVANTAGED BUSINESS ENTERPRISE THREE-
  YEAR GOAL FOR ALL FEDERAL TRANSIT ADMINISTRATION FUNDED PROJECTS FOR FISCAL
  YEARS 2022 THROUGH 2024. 112

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 RESOLUTION

  Report

REPORTS

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 21-55 – INTENTION TO CONSIDER GRANTING A PUBLIC UTILITY PIPELINE
  FRANCHISE TO HERAEUS METAL PROCESSING, INCORPORATED - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 21-55, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK DECLARING ITS INTENTION TO CONSIDER GRANTING A PUBLIC UTILITY PIPELINE
  FRANCHISE TO HERAEUS METAL PROCESSING, INCORPORATED; and schedule a public hearing
  for October 5, 2021. 618-16

  Report

  13. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – SEPTEMBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated September 2, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
